question: Are the source-level construction regimes mixtures of recurring local relational states inside individual objects, with non-random spatial organization and deeper agreement among previously frozen structural twins?

projection.rules: the two already-frozen parent blind rules; no new rule learning in this experiment

localStateDiscovery.selection: for each minimum context mass, standardize features and choose deterministic k-means solution with highest mean silhouette among non-empty solutions

stateSystemTests.withinSourceMixture: measure how often sources with at least two eligible observations contain more than one local state, plus normalized state entropy
stateSystemTests.spatialOrganization: within each source, connect each eligible observation to its nearest other observation by region-center distance; compare same-state edge fraction with deterministic within-source label permutations
stateSystemTests.sourceRegimeComposition: test whether the already-frozen two source-level construction regimes differ primarily in mixture proportions of the newly discovered local states
stateSystemTests.structuralTwinDepth: compare local-state histogram distance for the already-frozen 100 cross-lane twins against the full eligible cross-lane source-pair background
stateSystemTests.thresholdRobustness: repeat local-state discovery at every registered context-mass depth and record whether the same coarse state split persists

interpretivePosture: This experiment explicitly tests a generated theory. Failure, partial structure, state multiplicity, or unexpected state counts are all informative. The blind boundary protects the measurement; it does not prohibit theorizing from prior results.
